Thanks again for the time on Friday. Per our conversation, the next best step is a focused technical deep-dive to align on the migration/PoC architecture and hit a shared checklist (latency targets, data flows, security constraints). I want to include Marcus (solutions engineering) so he can review existing infra and propose a migration plan for the PoC.

Proposed 60–90 minute slots (PST):
- Wed Mar 4, 10:00–11:30 (best for our SE team)
- Wed Mar 4, 14:00–15:30
- Thu Mar 5, 09:00–10:30

Agenda (draft):
- 10 min intros & goals
- 20 min current infra & constraints (Acme)
- 25 min Redwood PoC architecture & mapping to your infra
- 20 min migration risks, data security, and SLA expectations
- 15 min open Q&A and next steps

Please confirm which slot works or suggest two alternatives. Also let me know if there are any other internal engineers or stakeholders we should include (networking, security, procurement). I'll send a calendar invite and a shared Drive folder with an initial migration checklist.

Thanks,

14:00–15:30 PST Wed Mar 4 works for us. Marcus will lead the technical portion. I've included a short pre-read checklist below and dropped the files into a shared Drive (link at the bottom). If you can upload the items you can ahead of the call, that’ll make the session productive.

Pre-read checklist (what we'd like from Acme before the call):
- Current inference topology diagram (png/pdf)
- Typical request/response sizes and token distributions
- Peak/average RPS and day/night variance
- Model formats (HF, ONNX, custom) and version(s) in production
- KV cache sizes and any prefix caching you use
- Relevant security constraints (VPC, IP allowlists, data residency needs)
- Any existing telemetry (latency percentiles, tail latency)

We plan to cover recommended mapping for PoC (dedicated vs hosted), quantization options, and a migration checklist. 

Calendar invite / Meet link: https://meet.google.com/xyz-arch-review
Shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/s/acme-poc-docs

Thanks — see you Wednesday.

Priya / Team —

Thu Mar 5, 09:00–10:30 PST works for Marcus/SE team. To address procurement: for most standard 30-day PoCs we run with a short SOW + mutual NDA; an MSA is not required up-front unless you have strict procurement controls. I’ll have our legal/ops send the standard PoC SOW template to procurement if that helps.

For the call agenda, I’ll plan to cover: PoC success criteria, data flows (ingest, inference, logs), fallback and rollback plan, quantization impacts on latency, and a rough timeline for cutover. If you can attach the infra diagram and sample telemetry before the call that will let me produce a proposed mapping in advance.

I attached an internal migration checklist and the diagram stub we discussed earlier.

Thanks — looking forward to it.
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
